features.name: any_comment_explicit_alternative_perspective
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly present its point as an alternative perspective or alternative way of looking at the issue (e.g. 'another perspective', 'alternatively')?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment itself explicitly signals that it is offering an alternative perspective/view/way of looking at the matter, e.g. 'another perspective', 'another way to look at it', 'alternatively', 'from a different angle', and then offers it. The signal must be in the commenter's own assertion, not merely in a quotation of the OP or others that the commenter does not adopt. Mere disagreement without explicit alternative-perspective framing gives 0. Use title/argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

h0: any_comment_explicit_alternative_perspective has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Rows with any_comment_explicit_alternative_perspective equal to 1 have a higher probability of OP view change.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view), tested at row level. Row-level 'any' presence is used; comments are unordered, with no per-comment outcomes, so it cannot show which comment persuaded. OC_comments may contain post-outcome text; the prompt excludes outcome announcements. Explicit framing is interpreted semantically beyond the example phrases; this is an assumption.
